summary: The EX40 is the renamed XC40 Recharge, a petrol-car-derived compact SUV that Australian reviewers consistently describe as sensible rather than exciting: comfortable, easy to live with and generously equipped, but behind purpose-built EVs on efficiency and packaging. April 2026 price cuts of $7,000 across the range dropped it to $69,990 and $74,990 before on-road costs, which reviewers treat as its strongest argument against a BMW iX1 or Mercedes-Benz EQA. Where opinion divides is whether an eight-year-old platform, a lapsed crash rating and the imminent EX60 make this a run-out bargain or a car worth waiting out.
pros: Both grades were cut by $7,000 in April 2026 to $69,990 and $74,990 before on-road costs, undercutting a BMW iX1 xDrive30 by roughly $8,000 and a Mercedes-Benz EQA 250+ by roughly $11,000 for comparable equipment

Volvo includes five years of complimentary scheduled servicing at 2-year/30,000km intervals plus five years roadside assistance, and covers the drive battery for 8 years/160,000km, so the only routine cost for the warranty period is tyres and electricity
Rated to tow 1,500kg braked as a Single Motor and 1,800kg as a Twin Motor, well clear of the 750-1,000kg typical of compact electric SUVs

There is only one equipment level and it is the top one: panoramic roof, 360-degree camera, Harman Kardon audio and Pilot Assist are standard, with paint, wheels and interior trim the only choices on the configurator

Volvo quotes a 28-minute 10-80 per cent DC recharge on a 200kW charger, and Australian testers recorded 17-18kWh/100km on the road after the 2024 motor and battery update cut the AWD car's consumption from nearly 24kWh/100km
cons: The five-star ANCAP rating it inherited from the petrol XC40 was datestamped 2018 and expired in December 2024, so the EX40 is now sold with no current crash rating -- an odd position for a car bought largely on Volvo's safety reputation

410 litres with the seats up trails a Kia EV6 (480L) and is barely half a Tesla Model Y (854L), and because the body was designed around a petrol drivetrain the front boot is only 31 litres and the load lip is high
The sole Ultra grade rides on 20-inch wheels; reviewers found the ride noticeably firmer than on the 19s the earlier single-motor cars wore, thudding over sharp bumps around town
Regeneration is a single on/off one-pedal switch with no selectable levels, where Hyundai and Kia rivals give you steering-wheel paddles

It is a run-out: the EX60 replacement is due in Australia in late 2026 or early 2027, EX40 sales fell about 40 per cent to 743 units in 2025, and two rounds of price cuts inside a year point to soft resale
